title: Ontario man shot by Edmonton cops; 31-year-old with big knife lunged at police
article: A man who allegedly ignored an officer's demand to drop a butcher knife and instead lunged at him was shot and killed by the officer Tuesday night.
Police said the incident happened about midnight in a suite of a six-unit residence in the south Edmonton neighbourhood of Royal Gardens.
John Peter Pavic, 31, died of a gunshot wound to the chest, according to an autopsy report.
Police say Pavic was formerly from Ontario, but did not specify a town or city.
About 8:30 p.m. Tuesday, police were called to the residence by the man who complained he was assaulted by a neighbour who kicked him out of a party in the building.
Police were called back at 10 p.m. by someone who said a man was walking around outside, waving a knife and yelling threats.
When police responded, the man went back inside his suite and refused to talk with them.
About two hours later, the tactical team got a search warrant and entered the man's suite, said Annette Bidniak, police spokeswoman.

"My information is that the officer that fired was actually cut with the knife," Bidniak said. "All we know is that (police) went in, demanded that he drop the knife, the altercation escalated and the man was shot."
Police also said there were several shots fired but wouldn't say how many.
A fatality inquiry is automatically called whenever police are involved in a death. Police will do an internal investigation as well.
Pavic's death was the third fatal shooting by a police officer in recent weeks in Western Canada.

Allan Thomas Symons, 53, of Lethbridge, Alta., died April 30 after being shot by one of two officers who responded to a 911 call warning of a man carrying a large knife. One of the officers confronted the suspect in an apartment building hallway.
On April 27, Melvin Wayne Bigsky, 33, was shot by police after being pulled over near Saskatoon.
Tuesday night's shooting was also the second confrontation with Edmonton police in a week to end in a death.
Last Friday, Kasim Cakmak, 37, died after Edmonton police pepper- sprayed him while trying to arrest him.
